🧬 Scientists Fuse DNA With A Computer Chip; Your Laptop Is Now, Technically, A Little Bit Alive

THE LAB — reported to a faintly breathing motherboard

SCIENCE — Researchers combined synthetic DNA with a semiconductor to build an ultra-low-power memory device that stores and processes information in the very same place — blurring the line between "computer" and "organism" and quietly giving your gadgets a biology to worry about.

"It's incredibly efficient," a scientist said, of a chip that now technically contains more genetic material than a small houseplant. Experts are thrilled about the low power draw and only mildly concerned about the day the laptop asks for a glass of water and a nap.

NEW!

🎁 Billionaire Gives Away A Powerful A.I. Model 'For Everyone'; Everyone Says Thanks, Then Reads The Fine Print

MENLO PARK — reported from behind a very generous curtain

MODELS — Meta released Glimmer, an open-weight AI model anyone can download and run themselves, with Mark Zuckerberg arguing AI should be "for everyone" rather than controlled by a handful of labs — a heartwarming gift, graciously offered by one of the handful of labs.

"Power to the people," the company said, handing the people a frontier model and, separately, the electricity bill required to run it. Enthusiasts celebrated genuine open access while gently noting that "free for everyone" and "runs on your laptop" remain, thrillingly, two entirely different promises.

WOW!

🚕 2,000 Robotaxis Descend On Europe; Ancient Cobblestone Streets Meet Their Confused New Overlords

SOMEWHERE WITH A ROUNDABOUT — reported from the back seat

AUTONOMY — A ride-hailing giant partnered with a Chinese firm to bring 2,000 robotaxis to Europe, unleashing a fleet of self-driving cars onto a continent whose roads were, for the most part, designed by a horse in the year 1400.

"They handle complex environments," the company said, of vehicles now facing the ultimate exam: a medieval one-way street, a double-parked delivery van, and a local gesturing with the full authority of someone who has lived here for sixty years. Pedestrians report the robotaxis are polite, cautious, and visibly bewildered by a roundabout that has no discernible rules.

⚡ A.I. Becomes The World's Hungriest Customer For Electricity; Politely Asks The Sun To Work Overtime

THE POWER PLANT — reported by flashlight

MARKETS — With every new model, chip, and data center, artificial intelligence has quietly become one of the planet's largest consumers of electricity — an appetite so vast that utilities have begun eyeing the sun itself with a mix of hope and open desperation.

"We're investing heavily in clean energy," companies insist, of an industry that now treats a gigawatt roughly the way most people treat a light snack. Analysts note the real bottleneck in AI is no longer talent or chips, but the ancient, humbling question of where on Earth all the electricity is supposed to come from.

NEAT

💾 Now That Anyone Can Run A Frontier A.I., Humanity Uses This Godlike Power To Generate Memes

A BEDROOM — reported at 1 AM, laughing alone

CULTURE — With powerful open models now downloadable by anyone, ordinary people finally hold world-changing artificial intelligence in their own hands — and are using it, overwhelmingly, to make pictures of their cat as a Renaissance king.

"The applications are truly limitless," one enthusiast said, having just asked a superintelligence to rewrite a breakup text as a pirate. Historians note this is exactly what happened with the printing press, the internet, and every powerful tool before it: first the revolution, then the memes, then mostly just the memes.
